title: Effective authentication
pass_criteria: Root login is disabled; every user/source Match context enforces the approved key/certificate or MFA chain; no unintended password-only route.
evidence: sshd -t; sshd -T -C for each approved context and root; approved authentication policy.
applicability: Always applicable to a server offering SSH.

title: Identity and key lifecycle
pass_criteria: Every privileged identity/key/CA has an owner, justified privilege, revocation path and current access review.
evidence: Redacted identity inventory, sudo scope, key/CA lifecycle and offboarding evidence.
applicability: Always applicable; non-SSH administration uses equivalent identity evidence.

title: Fresh access verification
pass_criteria: A new non-multiplexed session and required sudo action succeed after change; forbidden authentication is rejected in an authorized test.
evidence: Timestamped new-session receipt, effective forbidden-authentication policy and bounded negative test.
applicability: Always applicable when SSH is the management path.

title: Recovery and revocation
pass_criteria: The approved console/break-glass route and an access-revocation exercise meet the organization recovery objective.
evidence: Dated recovery/revocation exercise, responsible owner, credential storage and retrieval record.
applicability: Always applicable; do not perform a recovery drill during observational assessment.

title: Supported sources and coverage
pass_criteria: OS release, kernel track and repositories are supported, signatures verified and every software channel has an update owner.
evidence: Release/support evidence, repository signing configuration, entitlement status, third-party/runtime inventory.
applicability: Always applicable.

title: Fresh update inventory
pass_criteria: All required indexes have a successful refresh within policy; all pending/held packages are identified using both ordinary and new-dependency simulations.
evidence: Refresh receipt for every source, metadata age, apt holds, simulations, dpkg audit.
applicability: Always applicable; use vendor equivalents outside Ubuntu.

title: Patch execution evidence
pass_criteria: The approved pipeline or unattended policy has successful runs, intended origins, monitored failures and controlled restart/reboot behavior.
evidence: Effective allowed origins and periodic settings, timer/job state, successful transaction and failure alert receipt.
applicability: Always applicable; a managed pipeline is a valid alternative to unattended installs.

title: Remediation deadlines
pass_criteria: Every applicable overdue fix has an approved, unexpired exception; no unowned exposed vulnerability remains.
evidence: CVE/package mapping, exposure, owner, due date, exception approver and compensating control.
applicability: Always applicable; no open findings still requires the current inventory and policy.

title: Kernel track and boot capacity
pass_criteria: The approved supported flavour/meta-package is present; boot/root free space supports the reviewed transaction and recovery image.
evidence: Package/candidate records, vendor support track, bootloader type, disk capacity.
applicability: Always applicable to hosts; a container points to an identified host owner, not an automatic N/A.

title: Installed and active fix state
pass_criteria: Running kernel, installed fixed revision and actual next-boot selection are reconciled; livepatch claims name specific coverage.
evidence: uname -r; package ownership/version; actual bootloader entries; vendor advisory; livepatch evidence if used.
applicability: Always applicable to the assessed host. Livepatch itself can be unused without making the control N/A.

title: Verified reboot activation
pass_criteria: Required reboot is completed within policy and the intended kernel is active with working drivers, networking and workloads.
evidence: Changed boot ID, post-boot kernel, restart-needs check and workload acceptance record.
applicability: For a maintenance assessment. For a baseline audit, use a recent approved exercise; absent evidence is MANUAL.

title: Fallback boot recovery
pass_criteria: A retained recovery option has been exercised and can restore service within the approved recovery objective.
evidence: Actual fallback/recovery exercise, console access, application recovery and vulnerability re-triage record.
applicability: Always applicable; an image-replacement strategy can substitute for an older-kernel boot.

title: Approved exposure inventory
pass_criteria: Every listener maps to an owned service with expected protocol, family, source and destination; unused services are removed or explicitly excepted.
evidence: Service-exposure inventory and ss listener comparison.
applicability: Always applicable, including non-public hosts.

title: Effective host and platform policy
pass_criteria: Host rules, cloud/network policies and container forwarding permit only the approved paths across IPv4 and every deployed IPv6 path.
evidence: Effective rules, management-source restrictions, cloud/load-balancer evidence and container mappings.
applicability: Always applicable. Undeployed layers need an evidence-backed reason, not guessed absence.

title: Allowed and denied path proof
pass_criteria: Authorized probes confirm expected access and rejection from named management and untrusted vantage points, including deployed UDP services.
evidence: Source/destination/protocol/family matrix with live-listener positive and negative results.
applicability: Always applicable; no external vantage point means MANUAL for external exposure.

title: Firewall recovery
pass_criteria: The prior approved rules can be restored through a tested independent access path and required services recover.
evidence: Rollback exercise, saved exact policy and post-restore access/health evidence.
applicability: Always applicable; observational mode consumes existing evidence only.

title: Useful event coverage
pass_criteria: Persistent audit rules and authentication/privilege logs cover the approved event inventory and controlled events are retrievable.
evidence: Loaded and persistent rules, event inventory, redacted audit/authentication event examples.
applicability: Always applicable; alternative audit mechanisms require documented equivalent evidence.

title: Retention and pressure behavior
pass_criteria: Journal and audit-log limits separately match policy; rotation, free-space/queue alerts and failure actions are verified under safe test conditions.
evidence: Effective journald and auditd settings, retention calculation, rotation result, disk/queue alert exercise.
applicability: Always applicable; a configured limit alone is not a retention guarantee.

title: Authenticated central delivery
pass_criteria: Required event streams reach an authenticated central receiver; a failed certificate is rejected and a bounded receiver outage is detected and recovered.
evidence: TLS peer verification, unique marker receipt, audit-event receipt, negative TLS result, outage/recovery and queue evidence.
applicability: Always applicable for this production baseline; local-only logging is an exception, not N/A.

title: Actionable detection
pass_criteria: Synchronized timestamps, central access/retention controls and a routed alert with human acknowledgement meet policy.
evidence: Clock status, receiver retention/access policy, alert receipt/acknowledgement and response owner.
applicability: Always applicable; a lab sink is not proof of production alert handling.

title: Trusted desired state
pass_criteria: The approved baseline, scope and revision are stored independently of the host and tied to an authorized change.
evidence: Reviewed repository/artifact revision, external manifest digest, scope and approver.
applicability: Always applicable; a root-writable local manifest alone cannot pass.

title: Complete file inventory
pass_criteria: Approved paths match names, types, owners, permissions, symlink targets and file content; extra/missing files are detected.
evidence: Inventory comparison plus positive/negative regression evidence.
applicability: Always applicable; explicit exclusions must have owners and reasons.

title: Runtime and package drift
pass_criteria: Effective SSH policy, active firewall, enabled services, installed packages and kernel track match the approved inventory.
evidence: Versioned runtime/package/service inventories and independent comparisons.
applicability: Always applicable; filesystem hashes alone cannot pass.

title: Safe baseline promotion
pass_criteria: Missing/unreadable/unsupported input prevents baseline replacement; reconciliation preserves the approved record and exceptions expire.
evidence: Atomic promotion negative test, restoration test, approval record, drift ticket/exception expiry.
applicability: Always applicable.

title: Defined acceptance and recovery
pass_criteria: Named owner has approved success thresholds, observation window, rollback trigger, recovery objective and maintenance dependencies before change.
evidence: Completed change worksheet and recent application recovery evidence.
applicability: Always applicable.

title: OS and access acceptance
pass_criteria: Fresh admin access, intended kernel, completed package state, expected listeners, healthy critical units and logging pass after change/reboot.
evidence: Timestamped pre/post checks and unresolved-error list.
applicability: Always applicable; known pre-existing failures require an approved exception.

title: Workload acceptance
pass_criteria: A representative user transaction, background job and dependency path meet agreed correctness/latency/error thresholds during the observation window.
evidence: Actual transaction/job receipts and monitoring comparison to the recorded baseline.
applicability: Always applicable; a synthetic lab application does not certify the real workload.

title: Controlled rollout decision
pass_criteria: Canary acceptance, rollback rehearsal, staged rollout and final owner sign-off are recorded; failed gates stop advancement.
evidence: Release decision record with canary count, gates, rollback result and sign-off.
applicability: Always applicable; assessment alone never authorizes a production rollout.
